_comment: Canonical CSV serialisation contract shared by the backend (hexa.core.csv) and the frontend (DataStudioEditor/csv.ts). `vectors` pins how a single cell serialises (post-guard, post-quote); `rowVectors` pins whole-record shape (columns + rows -> full CSV, no BOM), which cell vectors cannot cover because each is wrapped in a fixed two-column row. Both export paths are asserted against this same file so the client path (small results) and server path (large results) cannot drift. Only JSON-representable values live here: type-specific branches that never cross the GraphQL wire (Python bytes/Decimal/datetime) are covered by backend-only tests. Numbers beyond the JS safe range are represented as strings, mirroring how NUMERIC/DECIMAL/bigint actually reach the frontend.

vectors.description: ordinary text that merely looks number-ish is not guarded
negative integer number is not an injection risk
big numeric string preserved beyond JS safe int
leading - on non-numeric text is guarded
number-looking but non-numeric leading - is guarded
value with a comma is quoted
embedded double quotes are doubled and quoted
guarded and quoted together (leading - plus comma)
object serialises to compact JSON, then quoted
array serialises to compact JSON, then quoted
non-ASCII text passes through literally (no \uXXXX escaping)
object with non-ASCII text stays literal in JSON (ensure_ascii=False), then quoted

rowVectors.description: header then one CRLF-terminated line per row
a lone empty field is written as "" (not a bare line) so single-column results stay byte-identical across paths
a lone non-empty field is not quoted
single column mixes quoted-empty and plain rows
an all-empty multi-column row is a bare separator, never quoted
